title: Al-Mani', the Preventer
tomorrow: Dadi's knee aches in the damp. what does she say to the ache?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Mughni, the Enricher, who gives more and gives enough. The line: he enriches. Today, the other side of giving: the thing that doesn't come.

The canceled flight. The party you weren't invited to that turned out to be a mess. The job that went to someone else. Yesterday's question: rain wipes out round two of the paint day. Bad luck, or harm held back? The tradition keeps two honest readings of a closed door, and they don't cancel each other out. Today, both get the floor.
screen: `THE CANCELED FLIGHT.` → `BAD LUCK, OR HARM HELD BACK?` → `TWO READINGS OF A CLOSED DOOR.`

segments.voice: Today's Name is Al-Mani', the Preventer, who withholds harm. The first reading says: the closed door is protection. The Qur'an, in Pickthall's words: "it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you, and it may happen that ye love a thing which is bad for you. Allah knoweth, ye know not." The Sufi teacher Ibn 'Ata'illah turned it into a riddle: sometimes He gives you by withholding, and withholds from you by giving. On this view, the rain on the paint day might be the gift. The second reading says: a closed door can also be a mirror. The Qur'an elsewhere ties some of what strikes us to what our own hands have done, and some scholars say a held-back thing is worth an honest look inward before you call it luck. On this view, maybe the paint day was rushed. Both readings are inside the tradition, and neither one turns into blame or into shrugging. And here's a line to tell a friend tonight: right after their prayers, Muslims say the Prophet's words, O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold. The word for withhold there shares its root with today's Name.
screen: `ONE READING: THE DOOR IS PROTECTION.` · `YE HATE A THING WHICH IS GOOD FOR YOU.` · `THE OTHER: THE DOOR IS A MIRROR.` · `NONE CAN GIVE WHAT YOU WITHHOLD.` · then, large: `HARM WITHHELD.`

segments.voice: Count back through the past year for things that didn't happen: a near miss on the road, a plan that fell through and turned out lucky, a sharp thing you almost said. Touch one finger for each. Let every finger be a quiet thank you, to God if you pray, or simply to the moment that held back.
screen: `THINGS THAT DIDN'T HAPPEN.` · `ONE FINGER, ONE THANK YOU.`

segments.voice: Al-Mani'. The Preventer, who withholds harm, and whose holding back can be part of His giving.
Your line: harm withheld, even on the days that only look like loss. See you tomorrow.

fork.setup: you lean toward 'every closed door is protection.' your friend says a closed door can also be a reason to look at yourself. what's the best case for your friend's side?
options: the Qur'an also ties some hardship to our own hands, so a look inward is honest.
closed doors always mean punishment, so feeling guilty is the right response.

fork.reveal: both readings live inside the tradition. the mirror view isn't about guilt; it asks for an honest look before calling it luck.

original.note: Arabic: the Preventer, from the traditional list of the Names; the same root is in the post-prayer words la mani'a, none can withhold.

trapdoor: what you thought: a God who says no.
what it means: the Preventer, who holds harm back, and whose no can be a form of giving.
what a scholar hears: al-Mani' is from the Tirmidhi list rather than the Qur'an's wording; la mani'a lima a'tayta is in Sahih al-Bukhari 844.

chat.meaning: The tradition reads a withheld thing two ways: protection (2:216), or a mirror. Al-Mani' withholds in wisdom either way.
